newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firmer as the short end staged a recovery, reversing some of recent heavy losses seen earlier this week.
Three-month December Euro Swiss futures traded on LIFFE ended firmer after dropping to as low as 98.12 in early trade, their lowest level since September 23.

"Basically people sold too much yesterday and many people also sold some in the first part of the session," said one Swiss-based dealer. He said fundamentals had not changed for the market. The Swiss National Bank, as expected, left its discount rate unchanged at 1.00 percent.
Traders said swap rates traders said swap rates fell after a pronounced rise this week.

The rates for two to four years fell by around nine basis points during the day on Thursday. One bank quoted two-year swaps late in the day at 2.25 percent. But this was still well above levels of as low as 2.05 percent seen a few weeks ago, one dealer said.
With respect to new issues, activity was very quiet.
"I think investors are focused on managing their risk and wondering if we are moving into a different interest rate cycle. It is not a great time to issue," one syndicate manager said.

Money market rates were above 1-1/2 percent in the afternoon, with tomorrow/next money quoted around 1-5/8 percent after the SNB announced no change in rates. This was a bit below 1-3/4 percent early in the day but still seen as firm.
Dec Comi medium-term bond up 30 at 110.20.
Dec Euro Swiss francs up eight at 98.24.
